title: Export fatally crashes: mu-migration helpers.php not loaded because vendor/autoload.php is missing
body:
## Bug

Calling `wu_exporter_export()` (synchronous or via admin UI) fatally crashes with:

```
Fatal error: Call to undefined function TenUp\MU_Migration\Helpers\maybe_switch_to_blog()
in inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/includes/commands/class-mu-migration-export.php:396
```

## Root Cause

`Site_Exporter::load_dependencies()` gates ALL file loading behind a check for `inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/vendor/autoload.php`, but that directory is **not tracked in git** and does not exist:

```php
public function load_dependencies(): void {
    $base_path = wu_path('inc/site-exporter/mu-migration');
    if (file_exists($base_path . '/vendor/autoload.php')) {  // always false
        require_once $base_path . '/vendor/autoload.php';
        require_once $base_path . '/includes/helpers.php';    // never loaded
        // ...
    }
}
```

Meanwhile, the `ExportCommand` and `ImportCommand` classes ARE autoloaded by the main Composer classmap (in `vendor/composer/autoload_classmap.php`), so they can be instantiated — but they crash immediately when calling helper functions that were never loaded.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
wp eval 'wu_exporter_export(2, ["uploads" => true], false);' --url=http://wordpress.local:8080
```

Or click "Export" on any site in the admin UI.

## Expected

Export creates a ZIP file.

## Actual

Fatal error — `helpers.php` functions undefined.

## Fix

`load_dependencies()` should load `helpers.php` and the command classes unconditionally (they have no external dependency). The `vendor/autoload.php` check should only gate loading of the `Alchemy\Zippy\Zippy` dependency (which is handled by the separate Zippy issue).

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php:1618-1632` — restructure `load_dependencies()` to always load helpers.php and command files; only gate vendor autoloader behind the file_exists check

## Severity

**Blocker** — export is completely non-functional.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---

title: Export/Import crash: Alchemy\Zippy\Zippy dependency missing — replace with native ZipArchive
body:
## Bug

The `Alchemy\Zippy\Zippy` library (required by mu-migration for creating/extracting ZIP files) is not available at runtime. The mu-migration `composer.json` requires `"alchemy/zippy": "0.4.8"` but:

1. `inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/vendor/` is not tracked in git (empty `git ls-files` result)
2. The package is NOT included in the main `composer.json`
3. `php -r "require 'vendor/autoload.php'; echo class_exists('Alchemy\Zippy\Zippy') ? 'YES' : 'NO';"` outputs `NO`

This means the `zip()` and `extract()` functions in `helpers.php` will throw a fatal error when called, even after the helpers loading issue (#1004) is fixed.

## Impact

- **Export**: The `zip()` helper uses `Zippy::load()->create()` to create the export ZIP — will crash
- **Import**: The `extract()` helper uses `Zippy::load()->open()` to extract import ZIPs — will crash

## Suggested Fix

Replace the `Alchemy\Zippy\Zippy` dependency with PHP's built-in `ZipArchive` class (available since PHP 7.4+, which is the minimum requirement). The `zip()` and `extract()` helper functions in `inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/includes/helpers.php` should be rewritten to use `ZipArchive` directly. This eliminates the external dependency entirely and makes the export/import self-contained.

Alternatively, add `alchemy/zippy` to the main `composer.json`, but this adds an unnecessary external dependency when `ZipArchive` can do the same thing natively.

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/includes/helpers.php:283-301` — replace `Zippy::load()` calls with `ZipArchive`
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/includes/helpers.php:7` — remove `use Alchemy\Zippy\Zippy;`

## Severity

**Blocker** — even after #1004 is fixed, export/import will still crash on the ZIP step.

title: WP-CLI export/import commands not registered: 'mu-migration' is not a registered wp command
body:
## Bug

The `wp mu-migration export` and `wp mu-migration import` WP-CLI commands are not registered, so users cannot export/import via the CLI:

```bash
$ wp mu-migration export all /tmp/export.zip --blog_id=2 --url=http://wordpress.local:8080
Error: 'mu-migration' is not a registered wp command.
```

## Root Cause

WP-CLI command registration happens at the bottom of each mu-migration class file (e.g., `\WP_CLI::add_command('mu-migration export', ...)` at the end of `class-mu-migration-export.php`). These files are only loaded via `Site_Exporter::load_dependencies()`, which is gated behind the non-existent `vendor/autoload.php` check (see #1004).

Even if #1004 is fixed, the command registration lines execute at file-include time, which only happens when `handle_site_export()` or `handle_site_import()` is called — too late for WP-CLI's command discovery.

## Expected

Users should be able to run:
```bash
wp mu-migration export all /tmp/export.zip --blog_id=2
wp mu-migration import all /tmp/export.zip --new_url=http://newsite.example.com
```

Or ideally, proper Ultimate Multisite CLI commands:
```bash
wp wu export-site 2 /tmp/export.zip --uploads --themes --plugins
wp wu import-site /tmp/export.zip --new-url=http://newsite.example.com
```

## Suggested Fix

1. Register the mu-migration dependencies and CLI commands early in the plugin lifecycle (in `init()` or `load_extra_components()`) so WP-CLI discovers them at boot time
2. Consider adding proper `wp wu export-site` and `wp wu import-site` commands as wrappers that call the underlying mu-migration commands — consistent with the `wu_` namespace convention

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/class-wp-ultimo.php` or `inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php` — load mu-migration commands during plugin init when WP-CLI is active
- `NEW: inc/apis/class-cli-export-import.php` (optional) — proper `wp wu export-site` / `wp wu import-site` wrappers

## Severity

**High** — CLI export/import is completely non-functional.

title: Export unavailable when Ultimate Multisite is not fully set up — blocks migration use case
body:
## Bug

The Site Exporter is completely unavailable when Ultimate Multisite is not fully set up (setup wizard not completed). In `inc/class-wp-ultimo.php:182-193`:

```php
if (WP_Ultimo\Requirements::met() === false || WP_Ultimo\Requirements::run_setup() === false || ...) {
    // Only loads Setup Wizard pages
    return;  // <-- exits before loading Site Exporter at line 584
}
```

The `Site_Exporter::get_instance()` call is at line 584, well after the early return. This means:

1. The `Sites > Export & Import` admin page is not registered
2. The export/import row actions on the WordPress Sites page are not added
3. The `wu_exporter_export()` / `wu_exporter_import()` functions exist but the action handlers are never hooked
4. CLI commands are not available

## Why This Matters

The export feature is specifically designed to work on the **WordPress default Sites page** (not the Ultimate Multisite Sites page) via `setup_wordpress_sites_integration()`. This is meant to enable migration FROM other solutions. But if Ultimate Multisite setup hasn't been completed, the integration is never loaded — exactly when migration is most needed.

## Expected

Export should work even when:
- Ultimate Multisite is installed but not fully set up
- The user is on a plain WordPress Multisite and wants to export sites before/during migration
- Running on a single site install (for migration to multisite)

## Suggested Fix

Move `Site_Exporter::get_instance()` (or at least the `setup_wordpress_sites_integration()` portion) to BEFORE the requirements/setup check in `init()`. The WordPress Sites page integration has no dependency on Ultimate Multisite being fully set up — it only uses WordPress core functions (`get_blog_details`, `wp_insert_site`, `wp_upload_dir`, etc.).

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/class-wp-ultimo.php:165-193` — move Site_Exporter initialization before the setup gate, or extract the WordPress integration into a separate early-load path
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php:40-61` — possibly split init into `init_core()` (WordPress integration, no deps) and `init_full()` (Ultimate Multisite integration)

## Severity

**High** — defeats the purpose of having WordPress Sites page integration for migration scenarios.

title: Import always deletes ZIP file regardless of user preference — isset vs empty bug
body:
## Bug

The `handle_site_import()` method has a bug on line 1601 that causes the "delete ZIP after import" option to be unreliable:

```php
$delete_file = isset($options['delete_file']);  // line 1601
```

This checks if the key EXISTS, not if it's truthy. Since `delete_file` is set by `handle_import_site_modal()` like this:

```php
'delete_file' => wu_request('remove_zip'),
```

If the toggle is OFF, `wu_request('remove_zip')` returns `false` or `''`, but `isset()` still returns `true` because the key exists. This means the ZIP file is ALWAYS deleted after import, regardless of the user's preference.

The WordPress Sites page import handler passes:
```php
'delete_file' => $delete_zip,  // from !empty($_POST['delete_zip'])
```

When unchecked, `$delete_zip` is `false`, but again `isset($options['delete_file'])` returns `true`.

## Expected

When the "Delete ZIP After Import" checkbox is unchecked, the ZIP file should be preserved.

## Fix

Change line 1601 from:
```php
$delete_file = isset($options['delete_file']);
```
to:
```php
$delete_file = !empty($options['delete_file']);
```

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php:1601` — change `isset()` to `!empty()`

## Severity

**Medium** — data loss (ZIP files deleted when user chose to keep them).

title: Import cron schedule has circular dependency — async imports may silently never execute
Security: Export ZIP files are publicly accessible without authentication
body:
## Bug

The export generates ZIP file names with the pattern `wu-site-export-{blog_id}-{date}-{timestamp}.zip` and stores them in the `wu-site-exports` folder inside `wp-content/uploads/`. However, this folder has no `.htaccess` or `index.php` protection, meaning:

1. **Direct URL access**: Anyone who guesses or discovers the export URL can download the ZIP file containing the full database dump, user data (including password hashes), and uploaded files
2. **Directory listing**: If directory indexing is enabled on the server, all exports are browsable
3. **No authentication on download**: The download URLs (`wu_exporter_get_folder() + filename`) point to raw files with no WordPress authentication check

## Verified

The export URL is constructed as:
```php
function wu_exporter_get_folder(): string {
    return WP_Ultimo()->helper->get_folder_url('wu-site-exports');
}
```

This returns a public URL like `https://example.com/wp-content/uploads/wu-site-exports/`. The "Download" links in the admin UI point directly to these public URLs.

## Impact

**Critical security issue** — exported ZIP files contain:
- Full database dump including `wp_users` table with password hashes
- All user email addresses
- Serialized user meta data
- Site options and settings
- Uploaded media files

## Suggested Fix

1. Store exports outside the web root (e.g., `WP_CONTENT_DIR/wu-site-exports/` with `.htaccess` deny rules)
2. Serve downloads through a PHP endpoint that checks `manage_network` capability
3. Add an `index.php` file and `.htaccess` with `deny from all` to the export directory
4. Consider adding time-limited signed download URLs

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/functions/exporter.php` — add directory protection on folder creation
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php` — serve downloads through authenticated endpoint
- `NEW: inc/site-exporter/class-export-download-handler.php` — authenticated download handler

## Severity

**Critical** — database dumps with user credentials accessible via public URLs.

title: Export always reports success even when it fails — no error handling
body:
## Bug

The export handler `handle_site_export()` calls `wu_exporter_export()` on line 575 but does not handle errors. `wu_exporter_export()` returns `true|\WP_Error`, but the handler always redirects with a success message regardless:

```php
// line 575
wu_exporter_export($site_id, $options, $background);
// line 577 — always shows success, even if export failed
$message = $background ? 'export_started' : 'export_complete';
```

Similarly, the AJAX handler `handle_export_site_modal()` on line 902-929:

```php
wu_exporter_export($site_id, $options, ...);
// Immediately sends success — doesn't check the result
wp_send_json_success([...]);
```

The synchronous export path (non-background) calls `do_action_ref_array('wu_export_site', ...)` which returns void, so there's no way to detect if `handle_site_export()` threw an exception or if the ZIP creation failed.

## Impact

Users see "Export completed successfully!" even when the export silently failed. No error feedback is provided.

## Suggested Fix

1. Have `handle_site_export()` return the export file path or `WP_Error`
2. Check the return value before sending success response
3. Add try/catch around the ZIP creation to surface errors
4. The synchronous path should use a return-value mechanism instead of `do_action_ref_array`

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php:556-588` — check `wu_exporter_export()` return value, redirect with error on failure
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php:902-929` — check return value in AJAX handler
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php:1493-1530` — return export result from `handle_site_export()`

## Severity

**Medium** — users get false success messages, cannot diagnose export failures.

title: Import URL-to-path conversion fails on HTTP/HTTPS mismatch — 'ZIP file not found' false negative
body:
## Bug

The `url_to_path()` private method in `Site_Exporter` (line 1367-1378) only converts URLs that start with the uploads base URL:

```php
private function url_to_path(string $url) {
    $upload_dir = wp_upload_dir();
    $base_url   = $upload_dir['baseurl'];
    $base_dir   = $upload_dir['basedir'];

    if (strpos($url, $base_url) === 0) {
        return str_replace($base_url, $base_dir, $url);
    }

    return false;
}
```

Problems:
1. **Protocol mismatch**: If the site uses HTTPS but the media library returns HTTP URLs (or vice versa), `strpos($url, $base_url)` will never match
2. **Multisite uploads path difference**: In multisite, the uploads base URL for the main site might differ from subsite uploads paths
3. **Returns `false` with no error**: When the conversion fails, it returns `false` silently. The calling code at line 1036 shows `"ZIP file not found"` — misleading when the real issue is URL-to-path conversion failure

There's also a separate `wu_exporter_url_to_path()` function in `inc/functions/importer.php:139-148` that does a different (better) URL-to-path conversion using scheme normalization, but it's not used by the admin import form.

## Impact

Import fails with "ZIP file not found" when the uploaded file URL doesn't exactly match the uploads base URL format (common with HTTPS/HTTP mismatch, CDN URLs, or custom upload directories).

## Suggested Fix

1. Normalize URL schemes before comparison (both to HTTPS)
2. Use the existing `wu_exporter_url_to_path()` function from `inc/functions/importer.php` instead of the private method
3. Fall back to `attachment_url_to_postid()` + `get_attached_file()` when direct path conversion fails

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php:1367-1378` — use `wu_exporter_url_to_path()` from importer.php or normalize schemes

## Severity

**Medium** — import fails silently for common URL format mismatches.

title: Import requires sed binary — fails in web/AJAX context for database prefix replacement
body:
## Bug

The mu-migration `ImportCommand::tables()` method (line 292-293) requires `sed` to be installed for database prefix replacement:

```php
// Terminates the script if sed is not installed.
$this->check_for_sed_presence(true);
```

And `replace_db_prefix()` (line 685-715) uses `sed` via `WP_CLI::launch()`:

```php
$full_command = "sed '$sed_command' -i $filename";
$sed_result = \WP_CLI::launch($full_command, false, false);
```

However, in the **web/AJAX context** (non-CLI):
1. `WP_CLI::launch()` is not available — the polyfill in `helpers.php` covers `db tables`, `db export`, `db import`, and `search-replace`, but NOT `sed` operations
2. The `check_for_sed_presence()` method calls `WP_CLI::launch('echo "wp_" | sed ...')` which will crash in web context
3. Even if `sed` is available on the system, the web user (www-data) may not have the same PATH

This means database prefix replacement during import is completely broken in web context.

## Impact

Admin UI imports (which run in web/AJAX context) will crash when importing a site that has a different database prefix from the target site — which is the normal case for cross-network migrations.

## Suggested Fix

Replace the `sed` dependency with a pure PHP string replacement using `str_replace()` or `preg_replace()` on the SQL file content. The `replace_db_prefix()` method does simple string substitution that doesn't require sed at all.

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/includes/commands/class-mu-migration-import.php:685-715` — replace sed calls with PHP str_replace
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/mu-migration/includes/commands/class-mu-migration-import.php:292-293` — remove sed presence check for web context

## Severity

**High** — database imports from different prefix sources fail in web context.

title: Database Import class has SQL injection risk, syntax error, and silent error handling
body:
## Bug

The `dropTables()` method in `inc/site-exporter/database/class-import.php:171` has an SQL injection vulnerability:

```php
$tables = $this->query("SHOW TABLES LIKE'" . $table . "%'");
```

The `$table` variable comes from the WordPress database prefix which is typically safe, but it's concatenated directly into the SQL query without any escaping or parameter binding. Additionally, there's a missing space before the quote: `LIKE'` should be `LIKE '`.

Also, the `query()` method at line 143-152 catches `Error` but not `PDOException`, which is inconsistent with the `connect()` method that catches `PDOException`.

## Additional Issues in the Import Class

1. **Line 182**: Multiple SQL statements in one query call — `SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0; DROP TABLE ...; SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=1;` — PDO may not support multiple statements by default (depends on `PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES`)
2. **No error reporting**: `openfile()` catches exceptions but only echoes them — in web context, these echoes go nowhere. Errors should be returned/logged, not echoed
3. **Memory**: The entire SQL file is read line-by-line which is good, but long multi-line INSERT statements could still cause memory issues

## Suggested Fix

1. Use PDO prepared statements or at minimum `PDO::quote()` for the table prefix
2. Fix the `LIKE'` syntax
3. Split multi-statement queries in `dropTables()`
4. Add proper error handling instead of echo

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/database/class-import.php:171` — fix SQL syntax and use proper escaping
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/database/class-import.php:182` — split multi-statement query
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/database/class-import.php:143-152` — catch PDOException

## Severity

**Medium** — SQL syntax issue plus defensive security hardening.

title: Synchronous export path uses do_action_ref_array incorrectly with extra ignored argument
body:
## Bug

The synchronous export path in `wu_exporter_export()` uses `do_action_ref_array()` incorrectly:

```php
do_action_ref_array(
    'wu_export_site',
    [
        'site_id' => $site_id,
        'options' => $options,
    ],
    'site-exporter'  // this 3rd arg is silently ignored
);
```

`do_action_ref_array()` only accepts 2 arguments: the hook name and an array of args. The third argument `'site-exporter'` is silently ignored.

The handler `handle_site_export()` expects `(int $site_id, array $options, string $hash)`:

```php
add_action('wu_export_site', [$this, 'handle_site_export'], 10, 3);
```

While the array values are correctly unpacked as positional params, the `$hash` parameter is never passed in the synchronous path, so it defaults to `''`. This means the export tries to delete a non-existent transient on line 1527:

```php
wu_exporter_delete_transient("wu_pending_site_export_{$hash}");
// hash is '' — deletes "wu_pending_site_export_" which never exists
```

This is harmless but indicates confused API design — the synchronous path shouldn't be using the same handler as the async path.

## Impact

Low — mostly code quality and potential for confusion. The extra `do_action_ref_array` argument and the empty hash transient deletion are both no-ops.

## Suggested Fix

1. Remove the extra 3rd argument from the `do_action_ref_array()` call
2. Guard the transient deletion in `handle_site_export()` with `if (!empty($hash))`

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/functions/exporter.php:45-52` — remove extra argument
- `EDIT: inc/site-exporter/class-site-exporter.php:1527` — guard with `!empty($hash)`

## Severity

**Low** — code quality issue, no functional impact.

title: Export/Import should support single-site WordPress installs
body:
## Enhancement

The export functionality should support single-site (non-multisite) WordPress installs. Currently:

1. The WordPress Sites page integration (`setup_wordpress_sites_integration`) only works in multisite because it uses `network_admin_menu`, `manage_sites_action_links`, etc.

title: Pending exports/imports queries use unprepared SQL and mismatched column aliases
body:
## Bug

The `wu_exporter_get_pending()` function in `inc/functions/exporter.php:197-208` constructs a SQL query with an unescaped LIKE pattern:

```php
$query = "SELECT meta_key, meta_value as site_id FROM {$table} WHERE meta_key LIKE '{$like}'";
return $wpdb->get_results($query);
```

While `$like` is hardcoded (not user input), the query is not using `$wpdb->prepare()` which is a WordPress coding standards violation and makes the code fragile if the pattern were ever made dynamic.

Similarly, `wu_exporter_get_pending_imports()` in `inc/functions/importer.php:84-111` has the same pattern:

```php
$query = "SELECT meta_key, meta_value as options FROM {$table} WHERE meta_key LIKE '{$like}'";
$results = $wpdb->get_results($query);
```

Both functions also have phpcs:ignore comments suppressing the `WordPress.DB.PreparedSQL.NotPrepared` and `WordPress.DB.DirectDatabaseQuery` warnings.

## Additional Issue

In `wu_exporter_get_pending()`, the column alias is `site_id`:
```php
$query = "SELECT meta_key, meta_value as site_id FROM {$table}..."
```

But in `class-site-exporter.php:395`, the pending exports are accessed as `$pending->options[0]` — meaning `options` property, not `site_id`. The column alias doesn't match the usage, suggesting either the query is wrong or the access pattern is wrong.

## Suggested Fix

1. Use `$wpdb->prepare()` with `%s` for the LIKE pattern
2. Fix the column alias to match actual usage

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: inc/functions/exporter.php:197-208` — use `$wpdb->prepare()`
- `EDIT: inc/functions/importer.php:84-111` — use `$wpdb->prepare()`

## Severity

**Low** — code quality and potential fragility.

title: t532: fix: publish pending site when admin manually verifies email and confirms membership
body:
## What

When an admin manually sets a customer's email verification to `verified` and checks the "Transition Membership" checkbox on the customer edit page, the pending site is not published.

## Why

`confirm_memberships()` transitions the membership from `pending` → `active` (firing `wu_transition_membership_status`) before `parent::handle_save()` persists the new `email_verification = verified` to the DB. The hook handler in `Membership_Manager::transition_membership_status()` reads the stale customer record, sees `email_verification = pending`, and bails out — so `publish_pending_site_async()` is never called.

## How

Add `$membership->publish_pending_site_async()` directly inside `confirm_memberships()` after `save()`. The method is an explicit admin override so it should be self-sufficient and not depend on hook ordering.

`publish_pending_site_async()` is safe to call redundantly — `publish_pending_site()` guards against double-execution via the `is_publishing` flag.

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `inc/admin-pages/class-customer-edit-admin-page.php` — `confirm_memberships()` method (~line 1321)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Saving the customer edit page with email set to verified + "Transition Membership" checked publishes the pending site
- No double-publish when the hook path also fires correctly (idempotent guard in `publish_pending_site()`)
- PHPCS passes on the edited file

title: Integration with Cyberpanel
body: Hi, I just integrated Ultimate Multisite with Cyberpanel. Everything works except the domain isn't created as an alias but as a separate domain. In Ultimate Multisite, everything looks fine, but when the site is visited, the default screen for empty Cyberpanel sites appears. When I delete the domain, it's also deleted in Cyberpanel. I tried doing it manually using WordPress's native domain mapping and adding it as an alias domain in Cyberpanel, and everything works as expected. Since there's no documentation yet on this process besides the interactive integration form, is there a step I'm missing? Or is it an integration error? My stack is a 2-core, 8GB RAM VPS on Hostinger with the Cyberpanel image provided by Hostinger.
